decision_rule: No model is assumed superior. A and B must be compared on equivalent scenarios and evidence.

assumptions.statement: MODEL A requires more orientation changes between corrugator output and conversion feed.
assumptions.risk: Potentially underestimates local transfer optimization if geometry differs substantially.

assumptions.statement: MODEL A has a more compact WIP footprint but could generate more queueing and reorientation overhead.
assumptions.risk: Needs real geometry to validate travel distance and bottlenecks.

assumptions.statement: MODEL B introduces a larger WIP capacity (120 + 255 cells) that may reduce starvation but increase inventory and space requirements.
assumptions.risk: Possible capital and handling cost increase; must be tested by WIP efficiency analysis.

assumptions.statement: MODEL B can improve natural flow and reduce direct transfers if the conveyor network is well coordinated.
assumptions.risk: Could worsen if the extra conveyor length and return path generate congestion.

benchmarks.statement: Corrugator OEE in stable industrial conditions is typically in the 80-95% band.
benchmarks.risk: Depends heavily on product mix and process stability.

benchmarks.statement: A robust WIP control policy can reduce starvation by 60-87% when logistics is synchronized.
benchmarks.risk: Applies to comparable plants; real plant variation may differ.

benchmarks.statement: A typical Ingetrans / AMR logistics configuration can reduce logistically induced downtime by 20-50% in critical loops.
benchmarks.risk: Depends on route, fleet size, and dispatch policy.

evidence_sources: Mission specification for PAIGE layout A vs B
